answer: Public-table bond: each identity locks 70 credits and files one row in the public cedar table: a willow-plot record sealed by a copper stamp. Auditors replay the table each epoch: a copied row from a rented-row ring, a reused copper seal, or one willow record claimed twice burns the bond. Forging 1,000 identities costs 70,000 locked plus 38,000 fees = 108,000 against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent files once, pays 38, keeps its bond.
